what: A registered per-cell breadth clause that a one-sided arm cannot meet makes PASS unreachable by construction. MEASURED 2026-11-19 on RQ-20261119-c5e8-01 (pooled 1d-ETF pullback direction): the rule required at least half of the cells with n >= 20 to pass their own cell rule, but the LONG and SHORT arms have 12-16 trades per cell (66-68 pooled over five cells), so the clause had no cell to apply to. LONG failed independently on folds (2/6) so the verdict stands, but the design was flawed and the harness wrote INDETERMINATE for the same reason (0 powered cells). Rule for future units (manager 2026-11-19): when an arm is single-sided (direction, side-filter) or otherwise splits the sample, register breadth on the POOLED population or on cells whose expected n per arm is at least the cell floor, and state expected n per cell per arm in the power block; do not copy the both-sides breadth clause. Applies to the authoring checklist for pooled-population units (STRUCTURE-EXITS-DEFAULT doctrine). No CI check and no new refusal is proposed (no new gates).
